32 An electron is in a uniform electric field of field strength 1500 V m–1.
What is the acceleration of the electron due to the electric field?
A
8.5  10–9
m s–2
B
1.6  10–5
m s–2
C
1.4  1011
m s–2
D
2.6  1014
m s–2

hints: Notice the field strength $E = 1500 \text{ V m}^{-1}$ acts on an electron, so recall the electron charge $1.60 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$ and mass $9.11 \times 10^{-31} \text{ kg}$.
Connect field strength to force with $F = EQ$, then connect that same force to acceleration with $F = ma$, giving $a = EQ/m$.
Check why one distractor is near $1.4 \times 10^{11} \text{ m s}^{-2}$ by testing what happens if you use the much larger proton mass in the same $EQ/m$ calculation.
walkthrough: Identify the given field $E = 1500 \text{ V m}^{-1}$ and the particle as an electron with charge $Q = 1.60 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$ and mass $m = 9.11 \times 10^{-31} \text{ kg}$.
State the force on a charge in a uniform field: $F = EQ$.
State Newton's second law for the resulting acceleration: $F = ma$, so $a = F/m = EQ/m$.

Calculate the numerator force $F = 2.40 \times 10^{-16} \text{ N}$, then $a \approx 2.63 \times 10^{14} \text{ m s}^{-2}$, which has correct units of $\text{m s}^{-2}$ and is very large because the electron mass is so small.

A.explanation: Far too small for an electron. It does not follow from $F = EQ$ and $F = ma$ with electron charge and mass.

B.explanation: Far too small for an electron in $1500 \text{ V m}^{-1}$. It ignores the very small electron mass of about $9.11 \times 10^{-31} \text{ kg}$.

C.explanation: This is about $1836$ times too small because it is the acceleration of a proton, using $m \approx 1.67 \times 10^{-27} \text{ kg}$ instead of the electron mass.

D.explanation: Correct from $a = EQ/m$ with $E = 1500 \text{ V m}^{-1}$, $Q = 1.60 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$ and $m = 9.11 \times 10^{-31} \text{ kg}$.
